critic_notes.rationale: The product of two industry z-scores is sign-degenerate — an unprofitable, expensive glamour firm (both z-scores strongly negative) receives a large positive score and enters the long leg, directly contradicting the stated claim that such firms are "penalized symmetrically," and the underlying profitable-value combination is itself a well-worn published composite.

A coherent state-conditional value signal whose gating is genuinely non-linear rather than a rescaling, though the 5% hurdle is arbitrary, the zeroed-out group is a bottom score rather than the claimed "neutral" one, and the economics are close to standard value-trap screening.

Gross-profits-to-enterprise-value is an established practitioner/academic factor (the EV-scaled cousin of Novy-Marx gross profitability and Gray-Vogel EBIT/TEV), and as a single accounting ratio it is a rediscovery rather than a cross-theme interaction.

Same sign-degeneracy defect as the other z-score product — expensive firms with deteriorating profitability produce large positive values and would be held long, flatly contradicting the reasoning's claim that they are shorted, and the ib/mktcap leg is additionally ill-behaved for loss-making firms.

Since rank(P/B) is a monotone inversion of rank(B/P), this "expectation-error gap" is arithmetically just an equal-weighted additive quality-plus-value rank composite — a standard construction relabeled with a mispricing story rather than a true interaction.

The MIN operator implements a genuine conjunction that an additive composite cannot replicate and the expected sign follows directly from the expression, but it is conceptually close to a standard profitability-by-value double sort and discards information about the stronger leg, so the incremental content over existing composites needs to be demonstrated empirically.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived CashFlowYield_Weighted_By_MarginImprovement — identical multiplicative structure (IND_RANK of a profitability TREND times a signed IND_ZSCORE valuation yield) with only the numerator (oancf→oibdp) and trend window (5→3) changed, so it tests sample depth rather than a new mechanism.

The debt-aware construction on both legs is economically coherent and plausibly less spanned by HML/RMW, but the EV denominator can go small or negative for net-cash firms, flipping the sign of the valuation leg in a way 1% winsorization will not fully control, so the sign discipline is fragile.

The earnings-quality-as-moderator channel is genuinely distinct from the level-of-profitability legs used so far and the sign discipline is clean, though it sits close to the well-documented accrual/value overlap (cash-flow-to-price subsuming both accruals and book-to-market), and the accrual weight and the (ib+dp)/P yield share the ib and depreciation terms, so the two legs are not fully independent.

The product of operating margin and sales-to-EV is, up to the rank transform, just operating-profit-to-enterprise-value — a long-published multiple (EBIT/EV) — so the stated claim that this "avoids restating an earnings multiple" contradicts what the expression actually computes, and it duplicates the EV-yield-times-profitability content of the SolvencyAdjustedProfit proposal.

Using the second moment of operating profitability as the conditioning weight is a substantively different channel from the level and trend weights already tested and directly addresses the value-trap diagnosis of generation 0, though a five-year VOL on annual data is noisy and will likely cut coverage toward the 0.08 range that already hampered the best gen-0 signal.

Dividend yield gated by profitability is essentially the commercially ubiquitous "sustainable/quality yield" screen, and the construction is internally inconsistent: dvc is zero for the large non-payer population, so the z-scored yield leg puts all non-dividend firms in the short leg, meaning the spread is payers-vs-non-payers rather than the cheap-vs-expensive comparison the hypothesis describes.

This is a one-term denominator tweak (dropping the cash subtraction) on the archive's existing SolvencyAdjustedProfit_x_EVYield with an identical moderator and identical economic story, i.e. a cosmetic re-parameterization rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the stated "diagnostic" value could be obtained more cleanly by winsorizing or flooring the EV denominator.

Capital intensity as the reason a pre-depreciation multiple misleads is an economically distinct moderator from the profitability-level, trend, volatility, solvency and accrual channels already tested, the expression matches the hypothesis and the sign discipline is clean, though dp/at is a noisy accounting proxy for maintenance capex (a capx- or ppent-based intensity measure would be a sharper test).

This is structurally the same short-side construction as the archived GlamourMultiple_x_ProfitFade with the multiple swapped from P/B to inverted cash-earnings yield and DELTA(MA) swapped for TREND, and the product of two non-negative ranks leaves the long (low-score) leg an uninterpretable mixture of cheap-improving, cheap-fading and expensive-improving firms, which is precisely the design that already produced a weak ls_talpha.

Testing whether the solvency and accrual-quality gates carry complementary rather than redundant information is a legitimate question that no single-moderator variant answers and the MIN conjunction is correctly specified, but it is an incremental stack of two archive components whose intersection will push coverage below 0.09 and risks an unstable portfolio rather than a genuinely new mechanism.

Recombining the own-history de-rating architecture with the best-performing solvency moderator and a cash-yield valuation state is a defensible levels-versus-own-norm test with genuinely lower HML loading, but both legs are non-negative so the low-score side conflates "expensive versus own history" with "weak interest cover," which will blunt the short leg exactly as in the generation-0 version.

The all-differences construction is genuinely new for this archive and the divergence story is coherent, but the reviewer's orthogonality claim is overstated: DELTA of a market-cap-scaled yield is dominated by the past-year price change, so the signal is close to a fundamental-trend-conditioned 12-month contrarian bet and must be diagnosed against momentum/reversal loadings before any alpha is credited to the divergence mechanism.

A clean factorial cross of the archive's two best-performing legs that is not a duplicate of any prior expression, but it is a mechanical leg-swap with no new economic content, so its main value is diagnostic (is durability leg-specific or additive) rather than genuinely novel.

Beyond being another cosmetic valuation-leg swap, the moderator NEG(xsga/(revt-cogs)) is numerically unstable and sign-flipping whenever gross profit is small or negative — exactly the distressed firms that drive the value-trap effect — so the "isolate the valuation channel" diagnosis is confounded by a badly constructed conditioner.

The switch from an asset-based to a margin-based durability hurdle is an economically meaningful distinction and guards against write-down artifacts, but the absolute 10% margin threshold is not industry-adjusted (unlike the IND_RANK legs elsewhere), so the count risks proxying for industry membership rather than franchise durability.

Replacing the bounded TS_RANK with a signed deviation from the firm's own five-year mean yield is a substantive repair that restores a genuinely two-sided short leg and is well-matched to the stated alpha-vs-slope diagnosis; the residual weakness is that unscaled yield deviations are mechanically larger for high-yield firms, so the leg partly reintroduces the cross-sectional value level it claims to demean away.

A cycle-averaged (Graham-Dodd style) earnings denominator is a genuinely new valuation construction in this archive and economically distinct from the spot yields tested so far, though the claim that coverage "stays high" is optimistic given five required annual lags, and averaged dollar earnings will tilt against fast-growing firms in a way that may masquerade as value.

Acceleration is a temporal dimension the archive has not touched and the expression's direction matches the stated inflection hypothesis, but a second difference of annual ROA is very noisy and closely related to published earnings-acceleration results, so the incremental information over the already-tested TREND moderator may be small.

Internally consistent and the highest-prior untested cell of the archive's moderator × yield grid, but it is pure recombination of two existing signals with no new economic content, so it is informative only as a confirmatory test rather than a genuine extension.

The expression genuinely computes what the hypothesis claims (mean ROA applied to current assets, priced against equity), it is a well-posed diagnostic for whether the winner was a stale-growth tilt, and the reviewer should note it collapses algebraically to average-profitability × assets-to-price — a decomposition close to the published profitability-scaled-value family — so the result must be interpreted against that benchmark rather than as fresh.

A clean single-factor change (denominator claim on capital) with the moderator and profit measure held fixed, but it is another grid cell in an already dense family, likely highly correlated with both parents, and the denominator omits cash so it is not a true EV yield.

This is the most genuinely new construct in the batch — a price-scaled cyclical-depression gap rather than another multiple — but the expected positive sign is a direct bet against the well-documented profitability premium (the signal is mechanically highest for firms with collapsing current earnings), so it must be read as a test of that tension and not a refinement of the normalized-yield winner.

The substitution of a within-industry margin count for the absolute 10% hurdle addresses a real confound (sector membership masquerading as franchise durability) with the valuation leg held constant, making this the most substantively motivated refinement here, though INDICATOR at a zero threshold on a demeaned variable will split roughly 50/50 each year and may therefore be a noisier gate than intended.

Peak-versus-mean is a legitimate alternative normalization anchor and the durability gate is the right guard against one-off windfalls, but TS_MAX will be very highly correlated with the five-year mean for the durable subsample the gate selects, so the marginal information over Signal 1 is likely small and the result should be judged on incremental, not standalone, evidence.

Because the durability gate is non-negative, SUB(oiadp, MA(oiadp,5)) is the exact negation of the already-evaluated MoatDurability_x_EarningsShortfallFromNormal, so the results are mechanically known (fmb ≈ +1.96, alpha ≈ +2.9%, t ≈ +3.34) up to winsorization asymmetry and the test adds no new information — the honest move is to re-label the sign convention of the existing signal, not spend a generation rerunning it.

A clean and coverage-cheap ablation that correctly decomposes the normalized yield into level plus deviation and asks whether the five-year smoothing earns its keep, though the valuation leg reduces to plain EBIT/P (a long-known anomaly) so the only novelty resides in the capital-intensity moderator already established in the archive.

Recasting the own-norm deviation as a scale-free bounded rank moderator on the proven normalized-yield leg is a legitimate structural question rather than a rescaling, but it overlaps materially with the already-tested TREND and ACCEL moderators of ROA, so the incremental information is modest.

Stacking the two best-performing moderators against the same valuation leg is a defensible complementarity-vs-redundancy test with no coverage cost, but multiplying two bounded weights compresses the effective cross-section and makes it the kind of incremental consolidation that will be hard to interpret if alpha lands between the two parents.

The stated mechanism is backwards — averaging historical per-share profits computed on smaller past share counts *flatters* serial diluters, whereas dividing averaged dollar profits by today's market cap already embeds the enlarged share base, so the expression penalizes exactly the opposite firms from those the hypothesis claims.

A coherent attack on the specific known failure mode of backward-looking normalization using a moderator dimension (top-line trajectory) the archive has not tried, though it works against the documented negative pricing of growth/investment, so a null or attenuated result would be as informative as a positive one and should be interpreted accordingly.

A single-operator denominator swap on the archive champion, but a defensible one — dp/sale is mechanically dp/at divided by asset turnover, so the test cleanly decomposes whether the champion's moderator works through capital consumption or through the asset-base denominator, though the incremental information over the champion is likely modest and the result will be highly correlated with it.

Asset turnover is a well-known DuPont-component predictor (Soliman 2008) so the leg itself is not novel, but its interaction with a mid-cycle-normalized yield is untested in this archive and economically distinct from depreciation intensity; note it is close to the reciprocal-complement of Proposal 1, so the two should be interpreted jointly rather than as independent evidence.

MIN(oiadp, MA5) is the one remaining cell of a three-point grid whose other two points (plain average 3.4%, MAX envelope 3.0%) already produced near-identical results, so the expected incremental information is small — but the conservative anchor does correspond to a genuinely different economic screen and the expression matches the hypothesis exactly.

Horizon-matching the accrual conditioner to the five-year valuation numerator is a coherent and non-cosmetic upgrade on the earlier one-year accrual gate, though the leg is a straightforward long-window Sloan accrual measure, the flow-numerator/stock-denominator scaling (5-year sum over current at) is internally inconsistent in units, and the oancf plus five-year window will bite coverage.

This is a pure monotone re-transformation of the champion that simultaneously and silently deletes every firm with non-positive mid-cycle operating profit, so any change in alpha confounds tail compression with a large sample-selection shift — exactly the coverage-driven "apparent improvement" the objective warns against — and the stated distress story concerns the sample screen, not the log itself.

Both legs are already in the archive (IntangibleCapitalIntensity_x_TotalCapitalEbitdaYield and the normalized earnings yield used by six prior signals), making this a mix-and-match grid cell rather than a new mechanism, and the stated attribution logic is weak since a middling result would be equally explicable by the known noisiness of accumulated-xsga proxies.

This is a pure functional-form tweak of the incumbent champion (graded rank weight replaced by a median indicator on the identical conditioner and identical valuation leg), so it is a cosmetic variant that will be near-perfectly rank-correlated with the existing signal within the retained half and adds no new economic content.

Adding spot and five-year-average operating profit is just the arithmetic midpoint of two already-tested anchors in the same family (spot t=3.33, MA t=3.55, plus MIN and MAX envelopes), and since MA(oiadp,5) and oiadp are highly correlated the blend is guaranteed to land between them — an interpolation, not a test of a new mechanism.

Swapping IND_ZSCORE for IND_RANK on the valuation leg is a normalization choice rather than an economic hypothesis, and while it genuinely reshuffles the short leg, it is the same two variables in the same multiplicative form as the champion and belongs in a robustness appendix, not as a new cross-theme signal.

The direction-of-travel of capital intensity is a genuinely untested dimension of the family's most productive conditioner and the expression matches the stated sign, but the reviewer should note that a falling dp/at is also a low-investment/asset-shrinkage proxy closely related to the asset-growth anomaly that FF5's CMA leg already spans, so a weak ls_alpha would be unsurprising and the hypothesis's "transitioning to asset-light" reading is only one of several interpretations.

Subtracting a one-year change in the dollar debt stock from a five-year average profit flow mixes incommensurate quantities whose scales differ by an order of magnitude, so the valuation leg will be dominated by net debt issuance scaled by market cap — effectively rediscovering the well-documented net debt issuance / external financing anomaly rather than testing a value-quality interaction.

The conditioner is the net share issuance anomaly (Pontiff–Woodgate, Daniel–Titman, and the composite-issuance literature), a first-order standalone predictor whose known sign will drive most of the product's slope, and it is mechanically correlated with the valuation leg because repurchases shrink csho and hence the market-cap denominator — so a positive result would not identify the claimed "buybacks at low multiples" interaction.

Pricing operating profit against a cash-netted market value is a coherent and genuinely untested fix to the champion's numerator/denominator mismatch, but the MAX(...,ceq) floor silently switches cash-rich firms from a market-based to a book-based denominator, creating a hybrid quantity whose cross-sectional ranks mix two different constructs and which should be diagnosed if the signal works.

This is a pure lookback-window parameter tweak (MA 5 → MA 8) on the incumbent champion with no new economic content, exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and the proposal's own reasoning concedes any gain is confounded with survivorship from the longer history requirement.

Internally inconsistent — oiadp is already operating income *after* depreciation, so SUB(oiadp, dp) charges depreciation twice and computes oibdp − 2·dp, which is not the "owner earnings" the hypothesis describes; it is also single-theme (the cross-theme conditioning leg has been dropped entirely), reducing it to a depreciation-penalized earnings yield rather than a cross-theme signal.

The conditioning ratio Δat/Σoiadp flips sign whenever cumulative five-year operating profit is negative, so asset-growing loss-makers receive the *highest* "discipline" rank — a sign pathology that winsorization and industry ranking do not repair — and what survives is largely the asset-growth/CMA investment anomaly already spanned by the FF5 benchmark and by the archive's IncrementalCapitalReturn entry.

The MIN conjunction of revenue expansion and margin improvement is a defensible non-additive refinement that neither already-tested parent reproduces and it targets the documented decliner-flattering weakness of backward-looking normalization, though both legs are recycled from prior entries and the 3-year growth requirement will cut coverage, so the bar for "beats RevenueGrowthGuard" must be genuine and not sample-driven.

Contemporaneous operating margin and ROA are near-collinear profitability measures already paired with this exact valuation leg elsewhere in the archive, so the construct is effectively a rediscovery of the standard quality-times-value composite (Novy-Marx/QMJ) dressed as an attribution test, and a MIN of two correlated profitability ranks is too weak an instrument to actually discriminate "capital intensity is special" from "any quality screen works."

A defensible additive combination of the archive's two strongest conditioners on an unchanged yield leg, but it is incremental engineering rather than a new mechanism, and the equal-rank sum will be highly correlated with each parent signal.

The differenced ratio is dimensionally incoherent (cash is a stock share, depreciation an annual flow rate, with cash typically the larger and far more dispersed term), so after IND_RANK it will be close to a monotone relabeling of the already-tested cash-intensity conditioner rather than the claimed "single economic quantity."

MIN is a genuinely non-linear alternative to the additive form and matches the stated necessary-conditions logic, though the archive already shows conjunctive MIN gating tends to shrink dispersion and dilute alpha relative to the single-conditioner parents.

This is the sharpest proposal in the batch: it pits two competing interpretations of the cash result against each other with opposite predicted outcomes, and is informative either way, with the caveat that cash entering both the conditioner and the denominator makes some mechanical reinforcement unavoidable and worth acknowledging in the diagnosis.

Testing liquidity net of the claims against it is an economically sensible refinement of the cash conditioner with clean bounded construction, though it partly overlaps the already-tested low-leverage conditioner and needs a stated handling of the zero-cash/zero-debt undefined case.

The nesting gives cash 50% and the other two 25% each, contradicting the stated "equally weighted rank index," and stacking a five-year average ROA conditioner onto a five-year average operating profit yield is largely a kitchen-sink re-aggregation of already-tested components rather than a new economic test.

validation_diagnostics.message: proposal expression does not use any variable exclusive to required theme: profitability (variables shared across the paired themes, e.g. common denominators like 'at', do not count as evidence for either theme)
